hints: Notice the diagram shows four blocks of thickness $h$ lying flat, so each uniform block has its centre of mass at $h/2$ above the table at the start.
Connect work done to gain in gravitational potential energy, $mg$ times the rise of the centre of mass for each block that is lifted.
Compare the lifts needed: one block can stay, while the other three must have their centres raised by $h$, $2h$ and $3h$ to reach the second, third and fourth layers.
walkthrough: Leave the bottom block where it is and lift the other three blocks onto it, so only three blocks gain height.
Work done against weight equals gain in gravitational potential energy, $W = mg \times$ vertical rise of centre of mass.
Initially each centre is at $h/2$. In the final stack the centres are at $h/2$, $3h/2$, $5h/2$ and $7h/2$.
So the rises are $0$, $3h/2 - h/2 = h$, $5h/2 - h/2 = 2h$ and $7h/2 - h/2 = 3h$.
Total work $= mg(0 + h + 2h + 3h) = 6mgh$, with energy unit $\text{J}$ checked from $m$ in $\text{kg}$, $g$ in $\text{m s}^{-2}$ and $h$ in $\text{m}$.
